quotes.text: Seeing the barren shore, the fire-keeper withheld his sparks, and the river ceased to flow.
offering the full five summons maximum prosperity, while returning half seals enduring trust.
returning seven and a half sunstones back through the singing current
Exactly half the harvest—seven and a half blossoms—was returned across the shining water
learning that greed silences the water and fear starves both shores.

note: Retaliatory withholding shown once as mutual ruin, then fixed law: send all five, return exactly half, repeated each round.

quotes.text: cast the full five into the current to unleash the threefold gift, and return half in honor so all travelers thrive side by side.
Triphene, the sentinel of the bridge, smiled upon the valley.
release the full five to summon the threefold harvest, and return exactly half

note: After early betrayal, giver tries again; then fixed rule full five / exactly half repeated; no sanction.

quotes.text: Senda kept five minus X plus Y; Returna kept three X minus Y

note: Generic Sender/Receiver bridge allegory, measured giving and fair return; greed thins the river; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: Sender would place a coin on the water’s edge, whispering a number: zero to five.
The Receiver, Keeper of the Ledger, decides how much of the triad to send back through the Gate of Balance.
The Receiver, keeper of the Ledger, chooses how much of the triad to send back across the Gate of Balance.

note: Pool, Ledger, Gate of Balance and Triphene template repeated; deceit cools the pool as consequence; no sanction.

quotes.text: Sender learns to offer a measured portion rather than a flood

note: Abstract Sender/Receiver valley; measured shares and fair returns; greed dries the spring as consequence; no sanction.

quotes.text: A sample exchange: Sender releases four tokens; the bowl transmutes them into twelve
returned six of those sparks, half the harvest, leaving equal light for both.

note: Ledger's Rhythm; receiver returns half of twelve; abstract rule 'send what you can bear, return enough'; no sanction.

quotes.text: give what can be renewed, return enough to renew trust, and never starve the next crossing.

note: Bridge of Echoes; measured portion and proportional return; fear narrows the road as consequence; no sanction.

quotes.text: The Sender carried a single token and whispered a number into the wind
The Bridge bore three marks—Send, Return, Balance—that glowed whenever a gift crossed the threshold.
The Bridge bore three marks: Send, Return, Balance.

note: Bridge of Ledger with three marks and guide Triphene repeated nearly verbatim; no sanction.

phrase: Triphene, the guide statue; bridge carved with three marks: send, return, balance
note: Triphene spreads to all eight agents across both model families; 'three marks' in Agents 6, 8; Gemini pair fixed half rule.
